chunks: O Sa'd! Learn the Quran, for the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection in the most excellent form that any creature has ever seen.

the creatures. The people will be in one hundred and twenty thousand rows — eighty thousand rows being the community of Muhammad, and forty thousand rows from the rest of the communities. Then it comes to the rows of the Muslims in the form of a man and gives the greeting. Then they look at him,

They say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous! This man is from the Muslims; we recognise him by his description and attributes, except that he was more intensely devoted to the Quran than us — that is why he was granted splendour, beauty, and radiance that we were not granted.' Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the martyrs. The martyrs look at him and say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Lord, the Merciful! This man is from the martyrs; we recognise him by his bearing and attributes, except that he is from the martyrs of the sea — that is why he was granted splendour and excellence that we were not granted.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the sea martyrs in the form of a martyr. The sea martyrs look at him and their astonishment intensifies; they say: This one is from the sea martyrs; we recognise him by his bearing

and his attributes, except that the island where he was killed was of a far greater terror than the island where we were killed — that is why he was granted splendour, beauty, and radiance that we were not granted.' Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the Prophets and Messengers in the form of a sent Prophet. The Prophets and Messengers look at him and their astonishment intensifies, and they say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous! This Prophet is a Messenger; we recognise him by his bearing and attributes, except that he was given abundant merit.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then they gather and go to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and ask him, saying: O Muhammad! Who is this? He says to them: Do you not recognise him? They say: We do not recognise him; this one is from among those upon whom Allah has not been angered,

upon him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says: 'This is the Proof of Allah upon His creation' — and he greets him. Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the Angels in the form of a close angel. The Angels look at him and their astonishment intensifies and becomes great upon them for what they see of his merit, and they say: 'Exalted is our Lord and Holy! This servant is from the Angels; we recognise him by his bearing and attributes, except that he was the closest of the Angels to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in station — that is why he was clothed in light and beauty that we were not clothed in.' Then it passes on until it reaches the Lord of Might, Blessed and Exalted. So he prostrates beneath the Throne, and the Blessed and Exalted calls out to him: 'O My Proof in

the earth, My truthful and eloquent Speech!' So he raises his head. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'How did you find My servants?' He says: 'O my Lord! Among them were those who preserved me and maintained me and did not neglect anything; and among them were those who abandoned me, took my rights lightly, and disbelieved in me — and I am Your Proof upon all Your creation.' So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'By My Might and My Majesty and the Loftiness of My Station! Today I shall surely reward based on you with the finest reward, and today I shall surely punish based on you with a painful punishment.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then the Quran turns its head in another form.' I said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! In what form will it return?' He said: 'In the form of a pale, altered man whom the people of the gathering can see. It goes to the man from our Shia who used to know it and debate with it against those of opposition. It stands before him and says: Do you not recognise me? The man looks at it and says: I do not recognise you, O servant of Allah!

Then the Quran says: 'I am the one who kept your nights awake and made your life laborious; you heard harm and were pelted with words because of me. Indeed! Every trader has now received his trade in full — and I am your backer today.' He (the Imam) said: 'So it goes with him to the Lord of Might, Blessed and Exalted, and says: "O Lord! O Lord! Your servant — and You know him best — was devoted to me, steadfast in me; he was made an enemy because of me, loved and hated for my sake." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Enter My servant into My Paradise, clothe him with a garment from the garments of Paradise, and crown him with a crown." When that is done with him, he is presented to the Quran, and it is said to it: "Are you pleased with what has been done for your friend?" It says: "O Lord! I consider this little for him — increase it with all goodness further." So He says: "By My Might and My Majesty, My Exaltedness and the Loftiness of My Station! Today I shall grant him five things along with the increase for him and for those who were at his rank: Indeed, they are youth who will never grow old, and healthy ones
who will not fall ill, and wealthy ones who will never become poor, and joyful ones who will never grieve, and living ones who will never die.' Then he recited

this verse: [44:56] They shall not taste therein death except for the first death. Sa'd said: 'I said, "May I be your ransom, O Abu Ja'far! Does the Quran speak?" He smiled, then said: "May Allah have mercy on the weak ones among our Shia — they are people of submission." Then he said: "Yes, O Sa'd! And the salat speaks; it has a form and a shape; it enjoins and forbids." Sa'd said: My colour changed because of that and I said, "This is something I am not able to say to the people." So Abu Ja'far said: "And are the people but our Shia? Whoever does not recognise
the salat has certainly denied our right.' Then he said: 'O Sa'd! Shall I let you hear the speech of the Quran?' Sa'd said: 'So I said,

'Yes, may Allah bless you.' So he said: [29:45] Indeed, salat prevents from immorality and evil, and the remembrance of Allah is the greatest. So the forbidding is speech, and immorality and evil are (two) men, and we are the remembrance of Allah, and we are the greatest.

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — epithet for God
key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: Proof/Argument of God — the Quran is God's binding proof upon creation
key_terms.ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ: Remembrance of Allah — here reinterpreted as the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.شُهَدَاءُ الْبَحْرِ: Sea martyrs — those who died in naval warfare

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the Quran on the Day of Judgment in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrated this extended eschatological vision to Sa'd al-Khaffaf, depicting the Quran as a living entity that will appear on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a man, progressively ascending through the rows of Muslims, martyrs, Prophets, and Angels — each group recognising it yet marvelling at its superior rank. The Quran intercedes for those who devoted their lives to it and the Imam reveals the living, speaking nature of both the Quran and the salat, concluding with a Quranic verse (29:45) reinterpreted to assert that the Ahl al-Bayt are 'the remembrance of Allah'.
